transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm just here because I've been feeling a little overwhelmed lately, but it's probably just normal stress, you know? I recently moved into a new apartment, and I was barely unpacked when I just... I don't know, I started saying yes to a lot of things all at once. 

I took on some extra client prototypes at work—I'm a digital designer—and then I agreed to do these mentoring sessions, which is great, really, but maybe a bit much? And then I also decided I needed to completely redesign my entire portfolio right then and there. It was like I felt this sudden urge to fix my whole life in one sprint, if that makes sense? I just wanted to be productive, but maybe I overdid it a little bit. Is it normal to get carried away like that when you're trying to get settled?
During this period, did you need less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Um, well, I guess my sleep was a little different, but it wasn't anything too crazy. I mean, for a few nights there, I think I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours? But honestly, I woke up feeling completely fine. I actually thought, you know, this is great, I have all this extra time to get ahead on my projects. It didn't feel like a problem at all, I just felt really energized. That's not a bad thing, right? I mean, a lot of successful people don't sleep much, isn't that true?
During that energized period, were you talking more than usual or feeling hard to stop once you got going?

Oh, um... I don't think so? I mean, I'm usually a pretty chatty person anyway, especially when I'm excited about work or a new project. 

I guess I might have been a little more enthusiastic than usual when I was explaining my portfolio ideas to my friends, but I wouldn't say I couldn't stop. I just had a lot of thoughts I wanted to share, you know? I hope I wasn't being annoying or anything. Does it sound like I was talking too much? I really try to be mindful of not dominating conversations.
During that energized time, did you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Um... I wouldn't say euphoric. That sounds a little extreme, doesn't it? I mean, earlier this month, I definitely felt... really good. Like, almost electric and upbeat, you know? Like everything was just clicking into place. 

But... I guess I also had moments where I wasn't so happy. It's kind of embarrassing to admit, but I would feel so great one minute, and then the next, I'd just... snap. Like, I yelled at a contractor I work with, and I even snapped at my sister over these really tiny delays. It just felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done, which I know sounds silly now. I'm usually really patient, I promise. I felt terrible about it afterward. Is it normal to feel so positive but also get a little short-tempered like that? I just wanted things to go smoothly, you know?
During that energized period, did it cause serious problems in your work or relationships?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it caused *serious* problems. I really try to stay on top of things, I promise. But... I guess, maybe there were a couple of little hiccups? 

I did, um... I ended up missing a design review at work. It wasn't on purpose, I just got so wrapped up in everything else. And, well, honestly, I've kind of been keeping to myself a bit lately. Avoiding my friends and my sister... I just feel a little embarrassed, I guess? I know I've probably seemed a bit scattered and unreliable to them, and I hate being that person. I really want people to know they can count on me. Does that make sense? I'm trying to get back on track, I really am.
About how many days in a row did that energized period last?

Um, let's see... I think it was maybe just a few days? Like, three or four, maybe? I wasn't really keeping a strict count, to be honest. It definitely wasn't a whole week or anything crazy like that. 

I just remember feeling really productive for a stretch, and then it kind of... faded out. I hope that's an okay answer? I know I should probably pay closer attention to these things, I'll definitely try to keep a better track of it from now on if that would be helpful for you.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, work is always a little stressful, right? Just the usual deadlines and trying to keep clients happy. But there wasn't any big, terrible event or anything like that. It just kind of... happened. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a better reason for it? I know it would probably make more sense if there was some clear trigger, but I really can't think of one. I try to handle stress pretty well, usually. I don't want you to think I just fall apart over every little thing.
For the past several months, have you been worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Um, no, I wouldn't say excessively. I mean, I worry a little bit, but doesn't everyone? Just about normal things, like making sure my designs are good enough or that I'm keeping up with everything. 

I really try to stay positive and not let things get to me. I don't sit around just worrying for no reason, I promise. I try to be really level-headed about stuff. Is it normal to worry a little bit about work and things like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea. I'm not a total worrywart or anything.
